payload.note: Pitch-over and the camera ladder (T13c/T15/T16/T30/T31). A flight is now a phase machine: ascent (physics replay) → gravity turn → Earth orbit → dotted transfer arc → lunar orbit → cargo drop → return → parachute, cross-fading between camera views so each mission zooms out one step and the Moon zooms back in. Budgets per mission: 10 s at mission 1, 21 s for the full Moon round trip, under the 30 s cap. The ladder re-scales: altitude, then distance to the Moon, then population toward 10,000. Zero console errors, 60–61 fps, sim PASS. T33/T34/T24: the readiness window owns the top-left on the ground and becomes a go/no-go board when idle; mission control and the gimbal take over the moment the flight starts. Task pool is 36 jokey items grouped into six assembly stages, read as live commentary. T35 optimization: static farm and pad layers cached to offscreen canvases, fills batched, off-screen ground culled. Pad 150 draws to 49, turnaround 232 to 140, desktop turnaround 55 fps to 61. Verified identical with the clock frozen: 0.06% of pixels differ, none by more than 64/255, all on cached-layer antialiasing seams. T14 retune: cost growth 2.55, equipment priced above the tier it unlocks, population 0.95 per tonne. A player who buys what they can afford reaches low Earth orbit on launch 14 and finishes in about an hour. T17 railgun: fires during the Moon cargo phase where the camera actually is, pays about 90 cents per resident, grows with the colony. T36–T39 + A1/A2: ten mishaps, the upper-right checklist, a square LAUNCH with its own clock, the rocket lifting off the pad, and one canonical journey geometry — Earth lower-left, counter-clockwise orbit, figure eight at the Moon.
